short.q: Write 7,206 in expanded form.
short.working: 1 mark for 7,000 and 200; 1 mark for 6 ones with no tens.

short.q: Write 583 in words.
short.working: 1 mark for "five hundred and"; 1 mark for "eighty-three" spelt correctly with a hyphen.

short.q: Arrange 605, 560, 650 and 506 from smallest to largest.
short.working: Compare hundreds first, then tens. 1 mark for each correct pair of positions, up to 3 marks.

short.q: Round 47, 342 and 995 to the nearest ten.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct rounding. 995 goes up to 1,000 because the ones digit is 5.

short.q: List all the factors of 36.
short.working: Pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. 3 marks for all nine factors, 2 marks for seven or eight, 1 mark for at least five.

short.q: Write the first five multiples of 9.
short.working: 1 mark for the first three and 1 mark for the last two.

short.q: State whether 1,468 and 3,975 are even or odd. Give a reason for each.
short.answer: 1,468 is even because it ends in 8. 3,975 is odd because it ends in 5.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct classification with a reason (2 marks) and 1 mark for referring to the ones digit.

short.q: Write 4, 6 and 9 as Roman numerals.
short.working: 1 mark for each. IV is 5 − 1, VI is 5 + 1, IX is 10 − 1.

short.q: Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5, 9, 13, 17, ... and state the rule.
short.working: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers (1 mark if only two are correct).

short.q: In the number 27,150, give the place value and the total value of the digit 7.
short.working: 1 mark for thousands; 1 mark for 7 × 1,000; 1 mark for the answer 7,000; 1 mark for clear working.

short.q: Find the first common multiple of 4 and 6 by writing the first six multiples of each number.
short.answer: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The first common multiple is 12.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct list and 2 marks for identifying 12.

short.q: Explain the difference between a factor and a multiple, using the number 6 as an example.
short.answer: A factor divides a number exactly: the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6. A multiple is found by multiplying: the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

short.q: Using each of the digits 4, 0, 7 and 2 once, write the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers you can make.
short.working: 2 marks for 7,420 (digits in descending order). 2 marks for 2,047 (a 4-digit number cannot begin with 0).

short.q: Write 4,605 in words and 305 in words. Then say which is greater.
short.answer: 4,605 is four thousand, six hundred and five. 305 is three hundred and five. 4,605 is greater.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct wording and 1 mark each for the comparison and its reason (more digits).

short.q: Add 4,236 and 1,528. Show your working.
short.working: Ones 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1 (1 mark); tens 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 (1 mark); hundreds 2 + 5 = 7, thousands 4 + 1 = 5, answer 5,764 (1 mark).

short.q: A shop earned Ksh 4,750 on Monday and Ksh 3,895 on Tuesday. How much did it earn on the two days?
short.working: 4,750 + 3,895. Ones 5; tens 5 + 9 = 14 write 4 carry 1; hundreds 7 + 8 + 1 = 16 write 6 carry 1; thousands 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. 1 mark for setting up, 1 for regrouping, 1 for the answer with units.

short.q: Add 3,568 and 2,276 and say how many times you regrouped.
short.answer: 5,844. You regrouped twice (ones to tens, tens to hundreds).
short.working: 1 mark for the correct sum, 1 mark for the carries, 1 mark for saying twice.

short.q: Estimate 5,382 + 3,617 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. Then find the exact sum.
short.working: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for the estimate 9,000, 1 mark for the exact sum 8,999.

short.q: Write the next three numbers in the pattern 2,000, 2,300, 2,600, 2,900.
short.working: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers.

short.q: A bus carried 5,684 passengers on Saturday and 3,749 on Sunday. Find the total number of passengers and check your answer by adding in the opposite order.
short.working: 2 marks for correct working with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with unit, 1 mark for the check.

short.q: Tabitha has 2,450 eggs. She gets 3,875 more. How many eggs does she have now?
short.working: Ones 0 + 5 = 5; tens 5 + 7 = 12 write 2 carry 1; hundreds 4 + 8 + 1 = 13 write 3 carry 1; thousands 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. 1 mark for method, 1 for regrouping, 1 for answer with unit.

short.q: What number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? Explain how you found it.
short.working: 1 mark for using subtraction, 1 mark for the working, 1 mark for the answer 2,318.

short.q: Start at 1,500 and add 1,000 each time to write a pattern of five numbers. State the rule.
short.working: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for five correct terms (1 mark for three or four).

short.q: Explain why the digit carried from the tens column must be added in the hundreds column when adding 3,568 + 2,276.
short.answer: Ten tens make one hundred, so the extra 1 hundred must be counted with the hundreds. If it is left out the answer will be 100 too small.
short.working: 1 mark for saying ten tens make a hundred, 1 mark for the carried digit being added in the next column, 1 mark for the effect of leaving it out.

short.q: Wanjiru saves Ksh 250 every week. Write how much she has saved after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 weeks. State the rule.
short.working: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for correct numbers.

short.q: Add 6,478 and 2,355 and check by estimating to the nearest ten.
short.working: 2 marks for the exact sum with regrouping, 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for the estimate.

short.q: Work out 4,000 − 1,236. Show how you regroup.
short.working: Borrow from the thousands so the number is 3 thousands 9 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones (1 mark). 10 − 6 = 4, 9 − 3 = 6, 9 − 2 = 7, 3 − 1 = 2 (1 mark). Answer 2,764 (1 mark).

short.q: A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books were left? Check your answer.
short.working: 2 marks for the subtraction with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units, 1 mark for the check.

short.q: Njeri had Ksh 5,000. She bought a school bag for Ksh 1,850. How much change did she get?
short.working: 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the answer with Ksh.

short.q: Work out 6,003 − 2,475 and check your answer by adding.
short.working: 2 marks for correct regrouping across the zeros, 1 mark for the answer, 1 mark for the check.

short.q: Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact answer.
short.working: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for 5,280, 1 mark for 5,287.

short.q: Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250.
short.working: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three numbers.

short.q: A water tank holds 1,000 litres. Each day the family uses 125 litres. Write the amount left after 1, 2 and 3 days.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct amount.

short.q: A stadium seats 9,000 people. During a match 6,450 seats are taken. How many seats are empty?
short.working: 9,000 − 6,450 with regrouping across zeros. 1 mark for the setup, 1 mark for regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units.

short.q: Subtract 2,718 from 5,432, showing every regrouping step.
short.working: Ones 12 − 8 = 4 (1 mark); tens 2 − 1 = 1 (1 mark); hundreds 14 − 7 = 7 (1 mark); thousands 4 − 2 = 2 (1 mark).

short.q: Explain how you can use addition to check a subtraction. Use 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323 as an example.
short.answer: Add the answer to the number that was taken away: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865, which is the starting number, so the subtraction is correct.
short.working: 1 mark for saying add the answer and the smaller number, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for saying the result matches the starting number.

short.q: A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875. How many were left? Estimate first by rounding to the nearest ten.
short.working: 1 mark for rounding 2,875 to 2,880 (6,500 stays), 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for the exact working, 1 mark for the answer.

short.q: Start at 10,000 and subtract 1,500 each time. Write the first five numbers of the pattern.
short.working: 1 mark for the correct rule and 2 marks for the numbers.
